Independent Study Confirms Environmental Advantage of PhotonAssay Analysis  May 04, 2026 We are pleased to announce that an independent assessment at SGS's Kalgoorlie, Australia facility has verified the sustainability benefits of PhotonAssay analysis. The study shows that, in comparison with fire assay, PhotonAssay Analysis dramatically lowers energy use, greenhouse gas emissions and hazardous waste, supporting the mining sector's goal to reduce supply chain emissions (Scope 3) from outsourced laboratory services. The assessment, which compared Photon Assay (PA) analysis and fire assay (FA), was conducted by GHD for Chrysos Corporation. GHD is a global, multidisciplinary professional services network providing clients with integrated solutions across advisory, digital, engineering, architecture, environmental and construction. The aim of the study was to understand the differences in emissions, energy use and waste. Using operational data from June 2024 to March 2025, the study found that PhotonAssay analysis consumed about ~9.81 times less energy per sample during analysis (~0.78 kWh) than fire assay (~7.64 kWh) ,with a total reduction of ~5.12 in average monthly energy consumption. Across all stages, including pre-analysis, PA used roughly ~6.71 times less energy per sample and ~5.06 times less energy per month. PA also produced about ~4.17 times less CO₂e emissions per sample and delivered ~5.32 times lower monthly CO₂e emissions than FA. Unlike fire assay, which generates significant Scope 1 emissions from natural gas fired furnaces, PhotonAssay analysis produces no Scope 1 emissions, relying solely on electricity and benefiting from grid decarbonization.
